question: Which three core areas come together to create nursing informatics?

options.C: Nursing science, computer science, and information science

explanation: Spot on! Nursing informatics blends nursing know-how with computer and information tools so we can handle patient data smoothly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why are health records so important as communication tools on the ward?

options.A: They provide legal evidence against hospital administrators
options.B: They calculate precise medication dosages for junior nurses
options.C: They replace verbal handovers entirely during shift changes
options.D: They share clinical data among the multidisciplinary care team

explanation: You got it! Health records keep doctors, nurses, and other team members on the same page about the patient's condition. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the main idea behind an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: The elimination of doctors from the data entry process
options.B: The restriction of patient files to a single clinic desk
options.C: The ability of different systems to share information
options.D: The permanent storage of data on physical paper folders

explanation: Exactly! EHRs are all about sharing data smoothly across different health settings so patient info travels where it's needed. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: How is an EHR different from just scanning a paper file into a computer?

options.A: It requires manual transcription for every laboratory test result
options.B: It stores information exclusively in offline local folders
options.C: It prevents any form of remote access via mobile devices
options.D: It actively shares data across multiple providers and departments

explanation: Well done! Unlike a static digital photo of paper, a true EHR lets different departments update and view live patient info together. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: What was one of the biggest headaches with old paper patient charts?

options.A: Excessive battery consumption during night shifts
options.B: Illegible handwriting and physical loss of documents
options.D: Instantaneous global sharing of clinical notes

explanation: Too true! Bad handwriting and misplaced folders caused endless stress and delayed care on the wards. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: When moving from paper to computers, what is a major hurdle nurses often face?

options.A: Managing an increased volume of physical storage cabinets
options.B: Eliminating the need for patient interaction entirely
options.C: Translating electronic codes back into handwritten notes
options.D: Developing adequate digital literacy skills for computer use

explanation: Spot on! Getting comfortable with new software and typing can feel overwhelming at first, but with practice, it gets much easier. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the job of the eMAR inside an electronic health system?

options.A: Digital tracking of prescribed drugs and administration times
options.B: Scheduling maintenance for hospital laboratory equipment
options.C: Recording human resource attendance and duty rosters
options.D: Tracking financial billing and patient insurance claims

explanation: Correct! The electronic Medication Administration Record helps you log when drugs are given, keeping patients safe at the bedside. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: How do clinical decision support tools help nurses during busy shifts?

options.A: They restrict patient access to their own laboratory results
options.B: They write complete nursing care plans automatically without input
options.C: They provide automated alerts for potential drug allergies
options.D: They manage hospital inventory and pharmaceutical purchases

explanation: You got it! These smart alerts act like a safety net, warning you about things like drug allergies before you administer meds. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: What best describes the reach of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR)?

options.A: It exists only in printed paper format
options.B: It connects every hospital across the entire country
options.C: It is restricted to a single clinic or hospital
options.D: It focuses exclusively on insurance billing data

explanation: Exactly! An EMR stays within one specific clinic or facility, acting as their digital version of the old paper chart. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which system is built to travel with a patient across different healthcare facilities?
explanation: Spot on! An EHR is designed for seamless sharing, so a patient's history can follow them across multiple hospitals or clinics. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: How do EHRs make a nurse's daily work easier at the bedside?

options.A: They replace the physician during patient ward rounds
options.B: They reduce time spent searching for physical charts
options.C: They remove all documentation duties from the nurse
options.D: They eliminate the need to perform physical assessments

explanation: Correct! No more running around hunting for missing folders—patient info is right there on the screen. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a major safety win when hospitals use electronic health systems?

options.B: Complete prevention of patient falls on the ward
options.D: Automatic diagnosis of complex surgical conditions

explanation: Well done! Clear digital orders and barcode checks help cut down mistakes when giving medications. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a major practical hurdle to setting up EHRs in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: A complete lack of trained software developers locally
options.B: Erratic electricity supply and unstable internet
options.C: Excessive availability of high-speed fiber cables
options.D: Strict government bans on computer usage in wards

explanation: So true! Power cuts and poor network connections make keeping digital systems running smoothly a real daily challenge. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge when rolling out EHRs in public hospitals?

options.A: Resistance to change from traditional paper users
options.B: Instantaneous acceptance by all veteran staff members
options.C: Concerns regarding data security and privacy
options.D: High financial costs for software and hardware

explanation: You got it! Change takes time, and veteran staff don't usually jump on board instantly—resistance is a normal part of the transition. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: What security rule makes sure staff only look at records they actually need for their work?
explanation: Spot on! Role-based access ensures you only see what's relevant to your specific clinical duties, protecting patient privacy. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is a safe practice for a nurse using a computer workstation on the ward?

options.A: Write their private password on a sticky note for easy access
options.B: Share their active login with junior colleagues to save time
options.C: Keep patient files open on screen for public viewing
options.D: Log out of the terminal when leaving it unattended

explanation: Always log out! Protecting your screen keeps patient records confidential and keeps your nursing license safe. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why are nurses considered key players in electronic health record systems?

options.A: They manage the financial budget of the hospital
options.B: They write all software code for hospital networks
options.C: They generate the bulk of daily patient documentation
options.D: They purchase the hardware devices for the wards

explanation: Correct! From vital signs to nursing notes, we input the largest share of data into the patient's digital chart. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h9)

question: What is an important responsibility for nurses when it comes to EHR data quality?

options.A: Negotiating software license fees with external vendors
options.B: Fixing physical hardware glitches inside the computer monitor
options.C: Ensuring all entered clinical information is accurate and timely
options.D: Encrypting the database servers against external cyber hackers

explanation: Spot on! Entering clear, accurate, and prompt notes ensures the whole healthcare team makes safe decisions for the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h9)
